validity.recommendation: Reclassify PipelineType from 'transmission' to 'gathering', and re-examine whether Fuel='Gas' / inclusion on the GAS tracker is still warranted. Every independent source describes this as a multi-product oilfield GATHERING system (crude oil + produced water + fresh water, historically also raw gas), not a gas transmission line. The owner's own current (2026) description of the asset omits natural gas entirely.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence is well confirmed (not a phantom): Pipeline News (Oct. 2018 trade PDF, 'Ongoing Projects: Construction Underway') carries a dated primary entry 'TAPROOT ROCKIES MIDSTREAM LLC - (9/18) / Project: Taproot Rockies Midstream System / Type: ...construction and operation of a multi-product midstream system in the DJ Basin comprised of natural gas, crude oil and produced water gathering, natural gas treating and processing and fresh water supply / Location: Weld County, CO / Completion: 4Q 2018 / Comments: System will initially serve a substantial acreage dedication from Bison Oil & Gas II LLC...'. Rigzone (Jun 2020) and Oil & Gas Journal (Sep 2019) both independently corroborate the system exists, is operated by 'Taproot Rockies Midstream' (an affiliate of Taproot Energy Partners), redelivers crude to Tallgrass's Buckingham terminal for ultimate delivery to Cushing, and is described by Rigzone as '...oil, produced water and freshwater pipelines' with NO mention of gas. The owner's own investment page (energyspectrum.com/investments/taproot-energy-partners/, live, dated '© 2026') describes current operations as '...a multi-service midstream system in the DJ Basin of northeastern Colorado that includes crude oil and produced water gathering and transportation as well as fresh water sourcing and distribution' - again with NO mention of natural gas. So: every source calling this a 'gathering' function agrees (Pipeline News 2018, energyspectrum.com 2026), which contradicts the sheet's PipelineType='transmission' - gathering lines collect from wellheads to a central point/terminal, which is exactly what all four sources describe (acreage dedications feeding into redelivery at a terminal), never a long-haul transmission function. On Fuel: the 2018 primary source lists gas as ONE of three products (gas/crude/water) gathered and treated on this system, but the two most recent independent sources (Rigzone 2020, and the owner's own 2026 page) describe the SAME system as crude-oil-and-water only, with gas dropped from the description entirely. I could not find any source stating this line moves gas today, or ever moved gas as its primary/defining commodity - the GEM row (on the GAS tracker, Fuel='Gas') may be capturing what is fundamentally an oil-and-water gathering system that incidentally also gathered associated gas circa 2018. This is a genuine classification/tracker-fit question, not a mechanical fix I can resolve alone - flagging PipelineType (high confidence: gathering, not transmission, per 2 independent + owner sources) and Fuel (real doubt whether 'Gas' should stand, or whether this asset is more properly tracked as an oil/water gathering system on GOIT) for a human decision. Checked the 46-row roster for a duplicate: the shared word 'Baja' with P0226/P2569 'North Baja Gas Pipeline' is coincidental - that system runs Ehrenberg, AZ to Baja California, Mexico and is unrelated; this Taproot system is a DJ Basin, Colorado oilfield asset. No duplicate. Opened 4 of the wiki page's 6 harvested citations (Pipeline News PDF verified live and read in full via pdftotext; Rigzone; OGJ). taprootep.com (http://www.taprootep.com/) returned HTTP 200 but is JS-rendered with no static content reachable by fetch - could not read it. Both BusinessWire press releases (2019, 2020) return HTTP 403 to scripted fetch; the archive.org Wayback availability API returned 429 (rate-limited) on two attempts this session and was not resolved - their content remains unverified beyond the citation context on gem.wiki itself, which cannot be cited per standing rule 1. Status='operating' is independently confirmed current as of the 2026 owner page (see fills).
